decisions.quote: While we expected to replicate this finding, we did not expect to find an overall effect of intensity. Nevertheless, both steady-state sequences and changing-state sequences presented at 75 dB(A) were clearly more disruptive than the same sequences presented at 45 dB(A). This finding was unexpected because in previous studies, no overall effect of intensity was reported, regardless of the auditory distractor type used (natural speech, music, spoken consonants, sine-wave tones) and of whether the intensity range was high (Colle, 1980; Tremblay & Jones, 1999) or medium to low (Ellermeier & Hellbrück, 1998; Schlittmeier et al., 2008).
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly pair their confirmation of an intensity-independent changing-state effect with an unexpected overall main effect of intensity that they contrast against the set of four prior studies, explicitly including Tremblay & Jones (1999). Although they later note that Tremblay & Jones (1999) held average sequence intensity constant, the paper's stated comparison across the two effects is mixed.

parent_objection: The first reply calls all four originals mixed from the unexpected overall intensity main effect. Immediately after its selected quote,the Discussion says results seem inconsistent at first,but on closer inspection the prior pattern is not clear. It states Colle experiments were not designed to evaluate intensity effects and are not directly comparable,and Tremblay/Jones held average intensity equal so those results do not allow conclusions about an overall intensity effect. In contrast,the actual preregistered replication target is independence of the changing-state effect from intensity,and authors explicitly say all seven prior experiments across the four originals show that finding and this was also the case here. Determine outcomes separately per original: does the unexpected main intensity effect actually contradict a finding each original reported,or is it an extension/not an applicable test in some originals? Do not apply a generic set comparison after authors qualify its scope. Low power alone does not erase an explicit original null finding or automatically establish uninformative; read each discussion comparison. All four original-target identities are accepted; preserve missing-target objects and settle their outcomes independently.
